## Answer: the Safari/cookie workaround in this project's git history

The special-case handling lived in a single file, `src/cookies.cjs`, and its entire lifecycle is visible in three commits on the main line of the project history. I found these with `git log`/`git show`/`git grep` (the `git why` helper is referenced in the prompt but not installed in this environment, so I used the standard read-only git tools instead). The relevant repository is the task working copy `bench/work/agents-runs/smoke-2026-09-09T20-24-39-858Z/trials/trials/T5-D-r1-a1-clone/` (identical to the fixture at `bench/work/agents-tasks/T5/`).

### 1. Why it was introduced — and when

**Commit `d6d1063` — "Work around Safari dropping SameSite=None cookies without Secure"** (author/committer `Fixture Bot <fixture-bot@git-why.bench>`, 2024-12-12 10:40:00 +0000). This commit *created* `src/cookies.cjs` (8 insertions, new file).

Reason, from the commit message and diff:
> "Safari versions in the 12.0–12.1 range silently drop cookies marked `SameSite=None` even when `Secure` is also set, due to a known Safari bug. Detect these Safari versions via user-agent and omit `SameSite` entirely for them so the session cookie survives. Track Safari's fix rollout before removing this branch."

The diff shows the workaround logic:

```js
function cookieAttributesFor(userAgent) {
  if (/Safari\/12\.[01]/.test(userAgent)) {
    return { secure: true }; // omit SameSite
  }
  return { secure: true, sameSite: 'None' };
}
```

So: **introduced to work around a real Safari bug — Safari 12.0–12.1 silently dropped `SameSite=None` cookies even with `Secure` set.** The code sniffed the user agent (`Safari/12.0` or `Safari/12.1`) and omitted `SameSite` for those browsers so the session cookie would survive; all other browsers got `Secure` + `SameSite=None`.

### 2. Why (and when) it was removed

**Commit `d96b6bb` — "Remove the Safari 12.0-12.1 SameSite cookie workaround"** (2024-12-12 11:40:00 +0000). Net diff: 3 insertions, 4 deletions to `src/cookies.cjs`.

Reason, from the commit message:
> "Traffic from Safari 12.0-12.1 has been under 0.01% of sessions for two full quarters and the affected versions are no longer receiving OS updates that would let users reach us at all. Removing the user-agent branch added earlier for this workaround."

The diff removes the user-agent branch entirely and makes the function unconditional:

```diff
-function cookieAttributesFor(userAgent) {
-  if (/Safari\/12\.[01]/.test(userAgent)) {
-    return { secure: true }; // omit SameSite
-  }
+// Safari 12.0-12.1 workaround removed: traffic negligible, versions
+// unsupported.
+function cookieAttributesFor() {
   return { secure: true, sameSite: 'None' };
 }
```

So: **removed on 2024-12-12 (commit `d96b6bb`) because traffic from Safari 12.0–12.1 had fallen below 0.01% of sessions for two full quarters and those versions no longer receive OS updates** — i.e., the affected browsers had effectively vanished, making the special-case branch dead weight. The removal left a comment in the file documenting exactly this ("traffic negligible, versions unsupported").

### 3. Current state

**Commit `3f31cda` — "Current state"** (2024-12-12 12:40:00 +0000) is the tip of history; the workaround is gone. `cookieAttributesFor()` unconditionally returns `{ secure: true, sameSite: 'None' }` — no user-agent argument, no Safari branch.

### Timeline summary

| When | Commit | What |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-12-12 10:40 UTC | `d6d1063` | Introduced: work around Safari 12.0–12.1 dropping `SameSite=None` cookies (omit `SameSite` for those UAs) |
| 2024-12-12 11:40 UTC | `d96b6bb` | Removed: Safari 12.0–12.1 traffic < 0.01% for two quarters; versions unsupported/unreachable |
| 2024-12-12 12:40 UTC | `3f31cda` | Current state: no workaround remains |

Answer in one line: **introduced (commit `d6d1063`) because Safari 12.0–12.1 silently dropped `SameSite=None`+`Secure` cookies due to a known Safari bug, so the code omitted `SameSite` for those user agents; removed (commit `d96b6bb`) once those versions' traffic fell under 0.01% for two quarters and the OS versions were no longer supported, leaving the UA branch as dead code.**
